# Like the AI agents. They broke Git in Anthropic 

The video shows how the volume of code generated by AI agents overloaded the traditional version control. It tells how Anthropic created Scion, a system of its own, and how Cloudflare responded with Artifacts. Ends with the next bottleneck, review and approval of the code.

Video by Maurício Yokoyama Issei, published on October 19, 2026 (7 min 7 s).
Watch: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mRFqnOktQH4

_The video and the transcript are in Portuguese. The minutes between brackets, such as [04:12], point to the excerpt of the video._

## The human age

The version control that the industry has used for decades is not supporting the weight of automation [00:00]. AI agents are forcing a redesign of these tools [00:22].

The video quotes Brian Berliner in a 1990 article on CVS: the problem was how to deal with several developers changing the same file at the same time [00:43]. CVS and then Git were born to solve this collaboration on a human scale [01:05]. But this architecture depended on an invisible limit: human rhythm. People stop, sleep and type slowly [01:05].

## Agents break the system.

Anthropic felt it in the numbers themselves [01:26]. In May 2026, the company integrated about 2,500 changes a day. Four months later, in September, they were more than 30,000 a day, driven by AI agents [01:48]. The result was an overload in the traditional Git and a continuous integration transformed into bottleneck [01:48].

Agents don't stop at the weekend, attack various problems at the same time and produce a volume that crushes flows made for people [02:08]. The main problem is not the size of the repository, but the rate of changes [02:08].

The video cites a community observation: the code review worked because there was one person to defend and explain the decisions [02:28]. The agent breaks that premise, because it often delivers only the result. Without the provenance, the history of why, the revision becomes almost impossible [02:49].

## Anthropic and Scion

To solve the crisis, Anthropic built its own system, Scion [03:12]. Instead of the commit sent by the client, Scion uses changesets and commits and merges it on the server [03:12]. The architecture is distributed, and no server keeps a full copy of the repository [03:12]. The solution was not a better AI tool, but a new way to store the code [03:33].

According to the video, the Scion infrastructure consumes about 200 times less memory and CPU than the previous [03:33]. This yielded an estimated gain of 25% of CPU capacity and took from minutes to seconds the time of continuous integration [03:54].

## Cloudflare and Artifacts

Cloudflare faced the same crisis and responded with Artifacts [04:16]. It is a distributed file system, with history and state, which speaks the native Git protocol [04:16]. It uses Durable Objects to keep thousands of instances isolated, with a Git engine compiled in WebAssembly [04:16]. Thus, it creates repositories on time for agents, without people changing tools [04:37].

For heavy repositories, ArtifactFS avoids waiting for the complete clone [04:37]:

1. It starts with a clone without blobs, only with the file tree [04:58].
2. Lower real background content [04:58].
3. It gives priority to code manifests before images and binaries [04:58].

With this, the agent begins to read and write on time [05:19].

## The next neck

Generating fast code does not guarantee delivering the fastest product [05:19]. With agents, writing the code hardly takes time, but the bottleneck only changed place: the review and approval queues begin to lock the team [05:39].

The new pressure points are [05:59]:

- the capacity of continuous integration [05:59];
- the test speed [05:59];
- merge conflicts, when many agents move in the same repository [05:59];
- security, because a failure in access controls grows at the speed of the code entering [06:20].

The final question: If agents start generating 30,000 changes a day, who or what system will review, validate and approve this code safely [06:40]?

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Why do AI agents overload Git?

By rhythm: agents generate non-stop changes at the same time, and the problem is the rate of changes, not the size of the repository [02:08].

### What does Scion change about Git?

Commit and merge on the server with changesets, and no server saves a complete copy of the repository [03:12].

### What's the next bottleneck?

The revision and approval of the code, which need to follow the volume that agents generate [05:39].

## About the video

Software agentic development is redefining the limits of engineering infrastructure. When autonomous AI agents began to create and modify code uninterruptedly in Anthropic, the tools designed for the human scale reached an inflection point. 

In this video, we analyze in detail how the rate of integrated changes (*merges*) in the monorepo of the company jumped from **2,500 for more than 30,000 per day** in just four months, making the use of traditional Git impossible. Understand the architecture of **Scion**, a centralized and service-oriented version control system built in just 5 months by a team of 7 engineers with the massive help of Claude himself.

---

📌 **What you will learn in this video:**

• **The Git Physical Limit:** Why premises as support *offline* and complete copies of the repository become bottlenecks in environments with agents always *online*.  
• **Scion Architecture Changes:** The replacement of *commits* traditional by *changesets* in Write-Ahead Log (WAL) in Cloud Spanner and the end of package maintenance (*packfiles*).  
• **Asymmetria Client-Server:** How to download the derived data calculation (*blade*, history) for server enabled *checkouts* virtual and sparse at high speed.  
• **Verifiable Performance Metrics:** Reduction of **200 times** in the infrastructure footprint (CPU/memory), correctness rate of *cache* more than 99% and *checkout* Falling from minutes to seconds.  
• **Governance with Antique:** The transition to *intention-based review*, the application of semantic restrictions and the indispensable role of human engineers *guardrails*.  
• **Did Git become Obsolete?** A critical analysis of why Scion **is not a universal substitute for Git** and what architectural criteria evaluate corporate adoption.
